connections.why: Relationships and identity lead into ideas of fairness and equality between people
Physical and mental wellbeing are taught together as two sides of healthy living
Sport and exercise overlap with free-time and leisure activities
Music is one of the most common leisure interests young people describe
Music, TV and film share the vocabulary of opinions and entertainment
Streaming, social media and gaming form the connected world of modern media
Technology skills link leisure use to studying and future work
Describing the local area naturally includes how people travel within it
Transport vocabulary is reused when talking about holidays and tourism
Where people travel and live connects to the natural world and environmental issues
Identity and home life feed into discussions of school, work and the future
Sound-symbol knowledge and vocabulary are essential for listening and dictation
Accurate grammar and vocabulary underpin open-response writing and translation
Vocabulary and pronunciation rules underpin the read-aloud and conversation tasks
Reading models the language structures students reproduce in their own writing
People-and-lifestyle vocabulary supplies content for the speaking conversation
Popular-culture topics are staple contexts for the picture task and role play
Travel and environment themes are frequent prompts for extended writing
Environmental texts are common reading-comprehension and translation sources
Wellbeing scenarios provide familiar contexts for listening comprehension
